title: Export runtime saturation signals (queue depth, token/sec saturation, memory pressure proxy) with bounded cardinality
creator: Christine Wong
project: Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding (Reliability Program)
description:
## Context
Overload protection (circuit breakers + load shedding) needs *runtime* signals that are both:
1) predictive of saturation (so we can shed early and avoid tail-latency blowups), and
2) safe to operate at scale (bounded cardinality, stable units, consistent semantics).

This ticket adds a minimal, high-signal set of saturation metrics exported from the serving runtime + scheduler. These metrics will be consumed by:
- Gateway admission/policy engine (ENG-4823) via the existing routing/control-plane signal path
- Dashboards + alerting (ENG-4826)
- Game day scenarios + capacity tuning sheets (Drive tuning sheet)

References:
- Confluence: Runtime architecture notes — runtime-backpressure-and-saturation-signals
- Drive: runtime-saturation-signals-notes
- Observability plan: overload-metrics-and-alerts-plan

## Goals
- Export queue depth and queueing delay proxies for both prefill and decode paths.
- Export token/sec saturation (actual vs target) as a stable, low-cardinality signal.
- Export a practical memory pressure proxy (KV cache pressure + allocator fragmentation proxy) without per-model-instance blowups.
- Enforce bounded metric cardinality by design (dim allowlist + runtime-side aggregation).
- Ensure signals are actionable for load shedding decisions (monotonic with saturation, low noise, well-documented).

## Non-goals
- Full per-GPU/per-worker introspection in default metrics (too high cardinality). We can keep deep diagnostics behind debug endpoints or sampled logs.
- Per-request tracing additions (handled elsewhere).

## Proposed signals (MVP)
All metrics exported as Prometheus (or OTLP->Prom bridge) from runtime pods, then aggregated.

### 1) Queue depth (prefill/decode)
**Metric names (proposal; align w/ observability naming conventions):**
- `redwood_runtime_scheduler_queue_depth{phase="prefill"}` (gauge)
- `redwood_runtime_scheduler_queue_depth{phase="decode"}` (gauge)

**Definition:** number of requests waiting to be scheduled for the phase.

### 2) Queue time proxy (optional but preferred)
- `redwood_runtime_scheduler_queue_wait_ms_p50{phase=...}` (gauge)
- `redwood_runtime_scheduler_queue_wait_ms_p95{phase=...}` (gauge)

**Definition:** moving window estimate over last N seconds for queue wait time. If histograms are too expensive/cardinal, export pre-aggregated p50/p95 gauges computed runtime-side.

### 3) Token/sec saturation
- `redwood_runtime_decode_tokens_per_sec` (gauge)
- `redwood_runtime_decode_tokens_per_sec_target` (gauge)
- `redwood_runtime_decode_utilization_ratio` (gauge; computed as actual/target; clamp [0, 2])

**Notes:**
- “target” should be configured per hardware profile/pool and updated with runtime config rollouts.
- If “target” is unknown, export only `tokens_per_sec` and leave ratio disabled.

### 4) Memory pressure proxy
MVP should avoid raw allocator internals with high variance. Export a composite set:
- `redwood_runtime_kv_cache_bytes_in_use` (gauge)
- `redwood_runtime_kv_cache_bytes_capacity` (gauge)
- `redwood_runtime_kv_cache_pressure_ratio` (gauge; in_use/capacity)
- `redwood_runtime_memory_pressure_score` (gauge; 0..100)

Where `memory_pressure_score` is a weighted score from:
- KV cache pressure ratio
- OOM/alloc-failure counters (rolling)
- optional fragmentation proxy (if available) such as “largest_free_block / total_free” (exported as ratio)

### 5) Backpressure events / shedding hints
- `redwood_runtime_backpressure_events_total{reason=...}` (counter)

Reason enum must be a *closed set* (e.g., `kv_pressure_high`, `decode_queue_high`, `prefill_queue_high`, `oom_recent`, `scheduler_overloaded`). No free-form strings.

## Cardinality rules (hard requirements)
We must be able to run this across hosted fleets without blowing up Prometheus/OTLP costs.

### Allowed dimensions (MVP)
**Allowed labels only:**
- `phase` (enum: prefill|decode)
- `region` (small set; injected by env)
- `pool` (GPU pool / capacity tier; injected by env)
- `model_family` (OPTIONAL; only if we can keep it to a tiny allowlist like llama|qwen|mistral and not per-version)

**Explicitly disallowed labels:**
- model name/version (anything like `llama-3.1-70b-instruct-2025-xx`)
- tenant/org/customer
- pod name, node name, gpu_uuid
- request_id, route, endpoint
- arbitrary error strings

### Aggregation strategy
- Runtime exports per-pod gauges/counters with only allowed dimensions.
- For any metric that would otherwise require high-cardinality (e.g., per-worker queue depth), aggregate inside the runtime process to a single value per phase.

### Sampling / update rate
- Gauges should update at ~1s (or 2s) cadence.
- Any expensive stats (p95 queue wait) computed over rolling window (10s) and updated every 5s.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Runtime exposes the above metrics on `/metrics` for hosted runtime pods.
- [ ] Metrics include only allowed labels; unit tests enforce label allowlist.
- [ ] A “cardinality budget” check exists in CI (simple regex/allowlist-based) to prevent introducing new labels without review.
- [ ] Metrics documented in a short internal README / Confluence snippet: definitions, units, expected ranges, and caveats.
- [ ] Dashboards can graph queue depth + utilization ratio + kv pressure and correlate with 429/503 overload responses (ENG-4826).
- [ ] Verified in staging load test that metrics track saturation (increase monotonically under burst scenarios) and do not spam time series.

## Implementation notes
- Prefer implementing metric registration in the scheduler module (single owner of queue state).
- Ensure counters don’t reset unexpectedly across hot reloads (process restart is fine; alerting should use rate()).
- For `memory_pressure_score`, keep the computation deterministic and documented; it’s a policy input and will be tuned later.

## Risks / open questions
- Histogram cardinality: if we use Prom histograms for queue wait times, bucket count * labels * pods may be expensive. Default to runtime-computed p50/p95 gauges.
- “Target tokens/sec” ownership: needs a config source of truth (likely pool-level config). If not ready, ship `tokens_per_sec` only in MVP and add ratio in follow-up.
- Model_family label: only include if we can guarantee it doesn’t explode as models are onboarded.

## Follow-ups
- Add a debug endpoint with per-worker details gated behind auth for deep incident triage (separate ticket).
- Tie `memory_pressure_score` into policy engine thresholds once we have tuning data.

2025-10-30 (Sofia Ivanova): Queue depth alone is OK but we also need a queueing *delay* proxy to avoid false positives when queue depth is high but draining quickly. Suggest computing rolling p50/p95 queue wait time in scheduler (no histograms exported).

2025-11-01 (Logan Wright): Please do NOT add pod/node/gpu labels. If we need drill-down, do it via exemplars or separate debug endpoint. Also request: add unit tests enforcing label allowlist to prevent regressions.

2025-11-04 (Julian Moore): Drafted metric names + minimal label set. Plan: export per-process aggregated scheduler stats, updated every 1s; queue wait p95 computed over 10s rolling window updated every 5s.

2025-11-07 (Omar El-Sayed): For memory pressure, KV cache pressure ratio is the cleanest and correlates well with decode slowdowns. Fragmentation proxy is noisy; ok to include only as part of `memory_pressure_score` but please keep raw fragmentation metric behind a flag.

2025-11-12 (Aisha Bello): For dashboards/alerts we need stable semantics: document units and expected ranges. Please ensure queue_depth is an integer gauge (not cumulative) and that tokens/sec is decode-only to start; we can add prefill tokens/sec later.

2025-11-18 (Julian Moore): Implementation in progress on runtime branch `runtime/metrics-saturation-mvp`. Added label allowlist helper + CI test. Remaining: wire kv cache capacity/in_use; currently only queue metrics are live in staging.

2025-11-21 (Julian Moore): Staging load test shows queue_depth + queue_wait_ms_p95 track burst ramp; no cardinality growth observed (time series count stable). Need to confirm memory metrics and then hand off to ENG-4826 for dashboard wiring.
